description: Sync all 7 mail accounts and reindex. Returns per-account ok/status.
name: sync

description: The triage queue: every inbox message not yet seen (by canonical hash), not noise. Read/unread is irrelevant — mail the owner already read on his phone still gets triaged exactly once.
name: new

description: Any notmuch query, newest first. Use to check for prior related threads before deciding a disposition (e.g. `from:sender@example.com`).
name: search

description: Full message headers + plain-text body. Takes either the `id` field from `new`/`search`, or a canonical `hash` — full, or a unique prefix such as the one stored in a todo's `source.hash`. A body longer than one answer comes back as its first part, with a line naming how many parts there are — pass `part` (2, 3, …) for the rest. Never guess at what a cut part left out; ask for the next one. `links` and every header travel whole on every part.
name: show

description: Record a decision about a message. disposition: 'todo', 'noise', or 'skip'. Pass todo_id when disposition is 'todo', matching the id you gave to `todo_add`; a 'todo' without it, or a 'noise' or 'skip' with it, is refused. Pass native_id as the `id` from the same new/search row this `hash` came from — it costs nothing and lets a later `show` resolve the hash directly instead of rescanning the maildir.
name: mark

description: Add a sender (bare email address) to the wholesale-ignore list.
name: noise_add

description:
Every currently-open todo, as {id, kind, category, priority, body, waiting_on, authored_by}. Use this to avoid creating a duplicate — if a message belongs to a topic already tracked here, link it to that todo's id via `mark ... --todo-id <id>` instead of authoring a new one. Complete view: it is the chain's own fold, not a scan of recent files, and the priority is evaluated as of right now rather than whenever a document was last compiled.

⚠️ IT IS ONE CHAIN'S LIST. Dedup against the chain you are about to write to: leaving `chain` out reads the owner's own todos, and `chain="suzatary"` reads this system's own work. Checking one and writing to the other is how a duplicate gets made.
name: list_open_todos

description: A short --stat summary of uncommitted changes, for a final sanity check before ending your session. You do not commit or push yourself — that happens afterward, deterministically, only if every store verifies.
name: git_diff_summary

description:
Propose a lifecycle event for a todo. kind is 'completed', 'cancelled', 'reopened', or 'tended' (no 'created' — todo authoring lives in the content verbs; no spec authoring). 'tended' is a pass at a RECURRING todo (its price holds a Recur): it was done again and stays open, so its price restarts from now. Never 'completed' for one of those.

Nothing is written to the chain: this files a card in the owner's Inbox, joining any open card about the same todo, and he taps it or answers no. `why` and `sources` are REQUIRED, as on `todo_add`; `sources` names the message that shows it happened. `todo` must be an id the chain already knows, or one an open card of yours adds; an unknown id is rejected as a likely typo.

`chain` is WHICH STORE the todo lives in and must match the one it was authored in — leave it out for the owner's own list, pass `chain="suzatary"` for this system's work.
name: record

description: The full lifecycle event stream for one todo from the chain, oldest first, as readable text (one line per event: kind, at, actor, note). An unknown id is not an error — it just has no history yet. `chain` picks the store the todo lives in.
name: history

description: Evaluate a priority spec at a moment against recorded history — your read-only window into the temporal logic. spec_json is a spec in the fpl JSON grammar (the same shape a todo's prioritySpec carries); it is parsed through the fpl JSON boundary (bad specs are rejected there). Returns the scalar `value` and a decomposable `explain` tree (every node its own fulfillment, Conj nodes their certified floor). Evaluated against trusted-only history as of `at` (defaults to now); provisional triage events do NOT count, so this shows the CONFIRMED belief. `chain` picks whose history it is evaluated against.
name: evaluate

description: Full fsck of the event chain (hash coverage, every parent present). Returns 'healthy' or the list of problems, one per line. `chain` picks which store is checked; the push path checks every one.
name: verify_chain

description: START HERE. Everything you need to act with understanding rather than classify messages in isolation: the triage contract (OPERATOR.md), the exact vocabularies the authoring verbs accept, and the secretary's memory (`memory`: the facts the owner had it keep, the newest when they do not all fit, then a short record of their own words in its conversations), which you read and never write; CLAUDE.md is already your project memory.
name: context

description:
Propose a new todo. Nothing is written to the chain: this files a CARD in the owner's Inbox, which he taps to make the todo or answers no. A later `todo_update` or `record` on the same todo joins the same card, so the Inbox holds one card for it.

`why`: REQUIRED — what the card is for, in a sentence the owner reads first.
`sources`: REQUIRED — what it rests on, comma-separated references, usually `mail:<hash>` of the message.
`todo_id`: 3-64 lowercase letters/digits, starting with a letter. It is the handle `mark --todo-id` and `record` use, so choose something you can reproduce (e.g. `permitfiling`).
`body`: the action line, one sentence, as Typst MARKUP: `*bold*` is bold, and a `$`, `@`, `#`, `*`, `_`, `<` or `[` you mean literally takes a backslash (`Pay \$40`). It is compiled before it is stored, without `html` or any file, and refused with the line and column when it does not compile. `detail` is the same. Every other field is plain text.
`rationale`: REQUIRED — WHY this priority, in one sentence. It is recorded as the comment above the number and is the only place the reasoning exists.
`kind`: 'todo' (needs `category`), 'ekaTodo' or 'suzateryTodo' (which set their own category — do not pass one).
`priority`: a whole percentage like '65%'. It is a FULFILLMENT: LOW means urgent, HIGH means satisfied or someday. Give exactly one of `priority`, `deadline_end_date`, `recur_every_days` or `periodic_every_days`.
`deadline_*`: use when the todo decays toward a date rather than sitting at a fixed number (`deadline_start_priority` defaults to 60%, `deadline_end_priority` to 5%). A deadline bounds WHEN, not the stakes: something merely moot afterwards (a form, a small recoverable cost) still floors around 60% on its last day.
`recur_every_days`: a chore done again and again (vinegar the toothbrush every two months). After every pass (`record` kind 'tended') the fulfillment runs from `cycle_from_priority` to `cycle_to_priority` over that many days, then holds; before the first pass it keeps the price it had. `periodic_every_days` is the same cycle on the calendar, whatever is done (rent). Both need both ends.
`waiting_on`: only when there is genuinely nothing we can do. One unblocking email we could send means leave it unset.
`source_*`: all four or none — the message this came from.
`date`: which day the todo is created on, YYYY-MM-DD, default the day it is made.
`parent`: the id of the todo this is a SUBTODO of. The parent's price gains a reference to this one in the same write, so its value composes this one's; without `category` this takes the parent's.
`chain`: WHICH LIST it goes in, and this is a decision, not a detail. Leave it out for the owner's own todos — mail, deadlines, people, money, travel. Pass `chain="suzatary"` for this system's own work: a gate that failed, a test that is flaky, a sync that broke, a verb that needs fixing. The test is who the todo is FOR. A todo lives in ONE chain and cannot be moved afterwards, because the Prodrome does not rewrite.
name: todo_add

description:
Propose changed fields on a todo that already exists. Nothing is written to the chain: this files a card in the owner's Inbox, joining any open card about the same todo, and he taps it or answers no. `why` and `sources` are REQUIRED, as on `todo_add`. Only the fields you pass change.

Changing `priority` (or a deadline, or a cycle — the same price fields `todo_add` takes, one of them) REQUIRES `rationale`: the comment above that number is the only record of why it is what it is. Passing `rationale` alone rewrites just the reason.

`clear_waiting_on` sets it back to `none` — use it the moment there is an email we could send, since `waitingOn` means nothing we can do.

`body`, `detail` and `detail_append` are Typst markup, checked as `todo_add` checks them. `detail_append`: a sentence to add under the existing detail, keeping its markup — use this, never `detail`, when the detail already exists; give at most one of the two.

`chain` must be the store the todo was authored in; there is no moving one between them.
name: todo_update

description: One todo as the chain holds it: its rendered block, its fields, and who last authored it when. Use it to check what you just wrote, or to see a todo's detail and source before deciding whether a new message belongs to it. `chain` picks the store it lives in.
name: todo_show

description: SEARCH THE SECRETARY'S MEMORY, read-only: the facts it keeps that contain `query` (plain text, any case), and the owner's own lines in its record that contain it, or a summary of nothing but those, newest first, each with its handle for `zoom`. Never the secretary's answers, a verb's answer or the box's notes. Use it before filing mail about a person, a place or a matter the owner may have talked about.
name: recall

description: OPEN A PART OF THE SECRETARY'S RECORD, read-only: `handle` is a part's `first+lines`, as `context`'s `memory` or `recall` shows it. Answers what is beneath it, each with its own handle: the owner's own line whole, a summary of nothing but their lines (`derived`, nobody's own words), or a span not summarised yet. Anything else (the secretary's answers, a verb's answer, the box's notes) stays shown by its kinds alone, however far you open it. Zoom before you file on what a summary says.
name: zoom
